subject: WaveHealth: Notice - Intermittent p95 latency elevation (hosted inference)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Thomas <grace.thomas@wavehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: WaveHealth: Notice - Intermittent p95 latency elevation (hosted inference)

Hi Grace —

Quick heads up: our monitoring detected an intermittent elevation in p95 inference latency for requests from WaveHealth beginning ~2026-11-18 08:45 PST. Impact appears as short spikes (2–6s) on a subset of long-sequence generation requests; overall success rates are unchanged.

What we know so far:
- Affected service: Hosted inference (us-west-1) routed to the shared pool.
- Impact window start: 2026-11-18 08:45 PST.
- Observed impact: p95 increased from ~380ms to 2–6s for ~7% of requests matching your workload profile (long-prefix + streaming).
- Initial mitigation: Automated prefix/KV cache hot-path has been toggled to reduce eviction aggressiveness. This has reduced spike frequency but not fully eliminated them.

Immediate customer-facing actions we recommend:
1) We have posted a short notice to our status page (link below) and will update as we confirm full remediation.
2) If you have critical jobs that cannot tolerate these spikes, let us know and we can route your traffic to a reserved pool (temporary) while we complete fixes.

We’re actively investigating root cause (initial signal points to unusual KV eviction churn under concurrent long-sequence workloads) and will follow up in ~90 minutes with an update. Attaching our preliminary timeline and a screenshot of the monitoring graph for your operations team.

Apologies for the interruption — we know latency variability is impactful.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261118_wave_incident_timeline.pdf (PDF), ops_screenshot_301.png (image)

Thanks Sean —

Appreciate the heads-up. Can you confirm:
- Is data integrity or model output affected?
- Rough ETA for a stable mitigation we can rely on?
- If we accept routing to a reserved pool, what is the expected lead time and cost delta?

Our primary engineering lead (cc'd) will be monitoring. We need to decide quickly about reroute.

— Grace
Director, Platform Engineering, WaveHealth

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:04:37 -0800
Subject: RE: WaveHealth: Notice - Intermittent p95 latency elevation (hosted inference)

Sean / Aditya —

Status update from the runtime team: toggling the KV eviction thresholds removed the biggest tail spikes (~>5s) within ~12 minutes, but p95 remains elevated (~1.0–1.6s) for a repeated subset of long-prefix, streaming calls. We have a candidate fix that reduces concurrent cache churn by spreading KV writes across a different local shard; we can deploy that as a canary to a small subset of nodes in us-west-1 now.

Recommended next steps:
- Deploy the canary to 10% of nodes for 30 minutes, monitor errors/latency.
- If stable, promote to 100% in rolling fashion (30 min window).
- Offer WaveHealth a temporary routing to our reserved pool (us-west-1-dedicated) for lower variance; provisioning and traffic shift would take ~25–40 minutes.

If Sean is OK with posting a status update, I'll hand you the short blurb for the status page.

— Monica
Lead SRE, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Thomas <grace.thomas@wavehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, WaveHealth Ops <ops@wavehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:32:10 -0800
Subject: RE: WaveHealth: Notice - Intermittent p95 latency elevation (hosted inference)

Grace —

Short answers:
- Model outputs and request payloads are not being altered; we have no evidence of data corruption or semantic regressions. Only latency variance.
- We are initiating a limited canary deploy of the KV-shard smoothing change now (Aditya's team). Expect initial telemetry back within ~15 minutes; we will escalate to full roll if green.
- Reserved pool: provisioning + route shift ~30 minutes once you authorize. I can initiate on your go/no-go. Cost delta: short-term hourly premium for reserved capacity; I'll have finance ops provide a ballpark in the follow-up (quick estimate ~1.8x unit cost for duration).

Status page: I’ve posted an incident entry: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/2026-11-18-wavehealth-kv-evict — short blurb below copied for visibility.

"Currently investigating elevated p95 latency for a subset of hosted inference requests in us-west-1. Mitigation work in progress; routing alternatives available for impacted customers."

Let me know if you want us to provision the reserved pool; otherwise we will proceed with the canary and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

Best,
Sean
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Thomas <grace.thomas@wavehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, WaveHealth Ops <ops@wavehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:07:00 -0800
Subject: WaveHealth: Incident update and next steps (hosted inference)

Grace / WaveHealth Ops —

Final update for this thread:
- Timeline: Canary (10% nodes) deployed 10:08 PST; within 9 minutes p95 for canaryed nodes dropped to ~380–420ms and error rates remained normal. We promoted the change to 100% at ~10:28 PST with a staggered roll; by 10:45 PST the p95 for your traffic returned to expected baseline.
- Root cause (preliminary): excessive KV cache eviction churn triggered by an atypical mix of large streaming requests + concurrent KV writes; the runtime shard allocation did not distribute high-write keys effectively.
- Remediation: the shard-smoothing change will be included in the next runtime stable release (v0.9.7) with an automated guard to detect similar churn patterns.
- Customer remediation offer: We will credit one week of hosted inference usage for the impacted window for WaveHealth. If you took the reserved pool route, we will credit the delta cost for that period as well.
- Postmortem: a detailed postmortem and timeline (root cause analysis, telemetry, follow-up actions) will be shared by EOD tomorrow. See attached preliminary timeline.

We appreciate your patience. If you'd like a quick call with runtime + SRE to walk the postmortem next week, I'm happy to schedule.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261118_wave_incident_timeline.pdf
